title: smtp: swap usenet-ipfs-sieve for sieve-native; license → MIT
description:
Replace the AGPL sieve dep in smtp with the new MIT native implementation.

What: crates/smtp/Cargo.toml, crates/smtp/src/session.rs (SieveCache type update), CLAUDE.md, root Cargo.toml

Algorithm:
1. crates/smtp/Cargo.toml: replace 'usenet-ipfs-sieve = { path = "../sieve" }' with 'usenet-ipfs-sieve-native = { path = "../sieve-native" }'; change license to 'MIT'.
2. session.rs: replace 'use usenet_ipfs_sieve::' with 'use usenet_ipfs_sieve_native::' throughout. No logic changes — API surface is identical by design.
3. sieve_admin.rs: same use statement swap.
4. CLAUDE.md: update license section — usenet-ipfs-smtp is now MIT; only usenet-ipfs-sieve (the old AGPL wrapper crate) remains AGPL and is no longer linked by any production binary.
5. Verify: 'cargo tree -p usenet-ipfs-smtp | grep sieve-rs' returns empty.
6. Verify: 'cargo tree -p usenet-ipfs-smtp | grep AGPL' returns empty (cargo tree doesn't show licenses directly, but grep for usenet-ipfs-sieve crate name).
7. cargo build --workspace succeeds.
8. cargo test --workspace passes.

Defensive rules:
- Do not remove usenet-ipfs-sieve crate from the workspace — it still exists as a standalone AGPL crate; just nothing links it in production.
- The old sieve crate's tests still pass (cargo test -p usenet-ipfs-sieve).
